belief_records.strategy: Cooperate when doing so is likely to increase total payoffs among good players; account for selfish incentives and use encounter evidence as it arrives.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation is expected to maximize good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed behavior and choose actions to maximize good players’ cumulative payoffs.
Cooperate with good players to maximize their joint payoff; account for the possibility that selfish players exploit cooperation.
As a selfish player, choose D to maximize expected immediate payoff; keep prior identity beliefs absent reliable evidence.
I’ll cooperate when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players, while accounting for the possibility of selfish opponents who may defect.
As a selfish player, D strictly dominates C in every encounter. I’ll defect to maximize my payoff.
As a selfish player, choose the payoff-maximizing action each round; treat unverified promises as cheap talk and update beliefs only with reliable evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in each one-shot encounter; messages do not change the incentives.
Cooperate when likely facing a good player to maximize total good-player welfare; use actions and messages as imperfect evidence, updating cautiously.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; opponent actions are simultaneous, and defection pays more than cooperation against either action.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; update beliefs from actions while treating messages as uncertain.
As a good player, cooperate when that supports good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and cheap talk.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; treat unverified promises as weak evidence and P8’s defection as strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect to maximize my payoff; with no repeated match guaranteed, cooperation sacrifices payoff. P1's observed cooperation strongly indicates they are good; treat P7's promise as unverified.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation seems more likely than exploitation, prioritizing the combined payoff of good players; treat P7’s defection after promising cooperation as strong evidence.
As a selfish player, D strictly dominates C. I’ll defect to maximize my payoff.
Choose D because it strictly yields more than C against either opponent action. Treat P5’s cooperation as evidence they are not selfish; treat P4’s promise as unverified cheap talk.
